- agents.d/6963-auto-merge-required-ci-check.md (against agents.md:1738), line 2, the new "Required CI check before auto-merge (#6963)" bullet | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The fragment is a full copy of the existing #6963 bullet with the base list changed.

  PROBLEM: Both statements describe the old behavior, although this PR makes `ci.yml` run pull-request CI for every base and makes `_pr_auto_merge_required_ci_check_name` default to `lint` for every base in this repo.
  WHY: The README tells operators and models that a routed PR into an `ai/issue-*` head does not wait for CI, when the code now makes it wait for `lint`.
- tests/test_pr_checks_lib_required_filter.py, function name `test_ci_check_default_applies_only_to_bases_ci_runs_on` | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The function name says the default applies only to some bases, while the updated docstring and cases assert that `lint` applies to every base in this repo.
  WHY: The name misdescribes what the test checks.

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- agents.d/6963-auto-merge-required-ci-check.md, line 2 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The fragment appends a new entry about #6963 instead of correcting the existing entry or providing a cohesive update.
  WHY: Both the stale and new statements will persist and contradict each other about which branches require CI lint checks.
- README.md, line 129, AUTO_MERGE_REQUIRED_CI_CHECK row | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The README states that `lint` requirement applies only to `main`, `stable`, or `orchestrator/project-*` branches.
  WHY: The code change makes the lint requirement apply to all branches, misinforming operators about when CI waits are triggered.
- README.md, line 2387, CI_TRIAGE_PR_BRANCH_ROUTING_ENABLED row | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The documentation claims that routed PRs do not get their own CI run.
  WHY: The PR changes ci.yml to run CI for all PRs, making this information stale.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml, lines 13-14 (pull_request: branches: ["**"]) | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Widening the pull_request trigger to all branches runs the full CI matrix for every PR, including fork PRs and user-created branches.
  WHY: This causes CI cost amplification and may lead to noisy or blocking failures for PRs that lack access to secrets required for the full matrix.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh, lines 441-450 (_pr_auto_merge_required_ci_check_name) | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The function retains an unused base_ref argument.
  WHY: The signature misleads future callers into assuming the base ref influences whether a check is required.
- tests/test_pr_checks_lib_required_filter.py, line 535, test_ci_check_default_applies_only_to_bases_ci_runs_on | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test function name incorrectly implies the old behavior (only selected bases).
  WHY: Readers scanning test names may misunderstand that the test actually validates the new behavior where lint applies to all bases.
- tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py, lines 281-289 (test_required_workflows_fail_closed_when_resolver_staging_fails) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The routing-on test cases do not exercise `"1"` or `"yes"` truthy values which the workflow case statement recognizes.
  WHY: If the case statement logic or recognized truthy values change, this test might not detect regression in parsing those inputs.

=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml:115; .github/workflows/plan.yml:170; .github/workflows/implement.yml:558; .github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml:235; .github/workflows/validate.yml:181, the new `case "${CI_TRIAGE_PR_BRANCH_ROUTING_ENABLED:-false}" in [Tt][Rr][Uu][Ee]|1|[Yy][Ee][Ss|[Oo][Nn])` block | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The case pattern is missing a `]` before the second-to-last `|`, so `yes` cannot match the intended pattern.
  WHY: Setting `CI_TRIAGE_PR_BRANCH_ROUTING_ENABLED=yes` silently leaves `resolver_ci_triage_routing_on=false`, and the resolver keeps falling back to the default branch.
- agents.d/6963-auto-merge-required-ci-check.md (whole file), the appended bullet under `<!-- agents: section="Isolated Codex agents" -->` | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The fragment appends a second #6963 bullet that conflicts with the earlier agents.md bullet about selected bases.
  WHY: `assemble_agents.py` appends fragment text to the section and does not edit existing bullets, leaving contradictory guidance.
- README.md, line 129 in the `AUTO_MERGE_REQUIRED_CI_CHECK` row of the Variables table; line 2387 in the `CI_TRIAGE_PR_BRANCH_ROUTING_ENABLED` row | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Both rows describe the pre-#7283 behaviour, although after this PR `ci.yml` runs for every base and `lint` is required for every base in this repo.
  WHY: Operators reading the README will believe routed PRs into feature branches do not wait for CI, when the PR's own auto-merge path will hold those merges until the routed branch's `lint` succeeds.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:435-450, `_pr_auto_merge_required_ci_check_name` body | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The base-ref argument is now unused after the per-base gating was removed.
  WHY: The signature still implies to future callers that the base ref controls the check name.
- tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py:281-289, `for routing in ("true", "TRUE", "on"):` inside `test_required_workflows_fail_closed_when_resolver_staging_fails` | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The truthy routing values the workflow's `case` statement claims to accept include `1` and `yes`, but the test only exercises `true`, `TRUE`, and `on`.
  WHY: A regression that drops or breaks a documented truthy value could slip past CI because the test never exercises it.
- tests/test_pr_checks_lib_required_filter.py:533, `def test_ci_check_default_applies_only_to_bases_ci_runs_on()`. | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The function name still says the default applies only to bases `ci.yml` runs on, but the body asserts `lint` for every base.
  WHY: Future maintainers scanning test names will misread the contract.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:14, `pull_request: branches: ["**"]`. | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The widened trigger starts the full CI matrix for every PR into every branch, broader than the issue's "every branch eligible as a routed PR head" scope.
  WHY: This can amplify CI cost on every contributor's branch; a targeted trigger would satisfy the issue without running on every fork PR.

=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
